findings.summary: The reason detector matches the common word 'because', so it lets the loophole back in.
findings.evidence: The plan takes as the reason the first criterion or out_of_scope item that contains a whole-word 'because', anywhere in the reading. 'because' is a very common word in criteria and out_of_scope entries, such as 'X is out of scope because it needs a records change'. So a candidate that writes 'expected 80%' plus any unrelated 'because' sentence passes an 80% replay. That is the 2026-10-28 loophole again: unchecked text in place of a measured number, now with a number attached. The reason the verifier sees would also be an unrelated sentence. The open question admits the detector is loose. The reading says the producer picks the detector, so the plan is free to make it stricter. Fix: Make the reason detector specific to why past readings should be refused. Require the item to contain a reason marker ('because', 'now asks', 'new required', in a documented const) and also mention past, earlier or previous readings or refusal (for example 'past readings', 'previous readings', 'refus'). Or require the reason in the same criterion as the declaration. Add a negative test: 'expected 80%' with an unrelated 'because' item, such as an out_of_scope 'records.rs is out of scope because ...', is held at the 10% limit.
findings.location: Decision 2 / Step 2 (reason detector: first item containing 'because', 'now asks' or 'new required')

findings.summary: A bare 'expected N%' parser reads quoted example numbers as a declared share.
findings.evidence: A bare 'expected N%' anywhere in a criterion counts as a declaration, and the first match wins. This job's own acceptance criteria quote 'expected 30%' and 'expected 80%' as test data, so under the new rule this job itself would declare 30%. Any reading that quotes an example percentage, or uses 'expected' in another sense ('coverage expected 90%'), would declare a share without meaning to. Fix: Parse only a form that names the replay, such as 'expected N% of newly refused readings' or 'N% of newly refused'. Or require 'expected N%' to sit in a criterion that also mentions refused readings. Add a test where a criterion quotes 'expected 30%' as test data and declares nothing, or document why that case is acceptable.

findings.summary: The criterion-4 test does not show that the real call site passes the reading's declaration into the view.
findings.evidence: `replay_view(&replay_record)` at run/mod.rs:2510 is where the verifier view is built. The plan's run/mod.rs test calls `replay_view(&record, &declaration)` with a declaration the test builds itself. It does not show that the call site at line 2510 builds the declaration from `ctx.reading` and not from a default. The existing go() test `replay_holds_over_threshold_rejects_the_job_and_records_the_list` shows the replay seam can drive the real path. Fix: Have the call site and replay_run share one helper that takes the reading, e.g. `fn reading_declaration(reading) -> ReplayDeclaration`, and test that helper. Or, if the fake reading's criteria or out_of_scope can be set in the go() test, assert there that the verifier inputs carry the declared share.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 4 / run/mod.rs line 2510 call site

summary: I read the replay code in reading.rs (lines 2744-2865), run/mod.rs (replay_view at 157, the verifier-inputs site at 2510, replay_run at 2814, the go() replay test at 4380) and briefs.rs (ReplayView, CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE). The functions and call sites the plan names exist, and the change is made where the fault starts. The plan replaces the phrase list with a declared share compared against the measured newly_refused/total in replay_is_held. It keeps the record valid by setting intended = declared && !held, since Replay::validate rejects held && intended. It correctly moves the deliverable from the non-existent brief.rs to athena-context's briefs.rs. The demonstrations for criteria 1-3 and 8 call the production replay and replay_is_held with the existing checker doubles and would fail under the old phrase rule. The main problem is soundness: the reason detector accepts any item containing the common word 'because'. A candidate declaring 'expected 80%' next to any unrelated 'because' sentence would pass an 80% replay, which brings back a text-based exemption close to the one this job removes. The detector should be tied to why past readings should be refused, and a negative test added. Smaller points: the bare 'expected N%' parser can read quoted example numbers as a declaration (this job's own criteria would declare 30%), and the criterion-4 test does not cover the line-2510 call site.
